newsitem.title: EGYPT: French team finds pyramid remains in Egypt desert.
newsitem.headline: French team finds pyramid remains in Egypt desert.

text.p: A French archaeological team in Egypt has uncovered the incomplete base of a pyramid built for an unknown pharaonic queen they say dates back to about 2300 BC, Egyptian newspapers reported on Monday.

They said the team, working in the vast ancient cemetery of Sakkara, also found a step inscribed in hieroglyphics with the name of Queen Ankhnes-en-Pepi, wife of Pharaoh Pepi II who is credited with the longest known pharaonic reign of 94 years.
The newspapers quoted the head of the French team as saying the discovery of the step augured well for finding a temple and pyramid dedicated to the little-known queen.
Team members were unavailable to give more details. Sakkara is also the site of the unique stepped pyramid of Zoser, who ruled between 2667 and 2648 BC.
